children: U.S. leading economic indicators edged lower in August, with consumer expectations remaining a significant strain on the Index.
The Leading Economic Index, or LEI, published by research group The Conference Board, fell by 0.1% to 99.5, following an increase of 0.2% in July.
"The US LEI receded slightly in August, the first monthly decline since March of this year," said Justyna Zabinska-La Monica, a senior manager at The Conference Board.
The LEI's six-month growth was down 0.1% between February and August 2026, a much smaller rate of decline compared with a 0.6% decline over the previous six months.

While the economy is still expanding, growth is expected to slow, The Conference Board said. Forecasts real GDP to increase at a 1.9% rate in 2026, with the outlook for 2027 downwardly revised to 1.8% from 1.9%.

The LEI is meant as a predictive index. It is based on 10 components, among them manufacturers' new orders, building permits for new private housing units, stock prices and consumer expectations, and aims to signal shifts in the business cycle.
